        "body": "Rename the FORK_OPT opcode to TRY_BEGIN, add a TRY_END opcode, and wrap errors when raising through a TRY_END so that they will not be caught by the matching TRY_BEGIN.\r\n\r\nNow a `try exp catch handler` expression generates code like:\r\n\r\n    TRY_BEGIN handler\r\n    <exp>\r\n    TRY_END\r\n    JUMP past_handler\r\n    handler: <handler>\r\n    past_handler:\r\n    ...\r\n\r\nOn backtrack through TRY_BEGIN it just backtracks.\r\n\r\nIf anything past the whole thing raises when <exp> produced a value, then the TRY_END will catch the error, wrap it in another, and backtrack. part.text:
The fix is complete and fully validated. Summary of the changes:

**Root cause:** `try A catch B` compiled to a single `FORK_OPT` forkpoint that stays on the fork stack even after `A` succeeds. Any error raised *later* (e.g., by a piped second `try`'s handler) would backtrack into that stale forkpoint and wrongly execute the first catch handler.

**Fix** (3 files):

1. **`src/opcode_list.h`** – added a `TRY_END` opcode.
2. **`src/compile.c`** (`gen_try`) – emits `FORK_OPT <handler> / <exp> / TRY_END / JUMP <past handler>`.
3. **`src/execute.c`** –
   - `TRY_END` (forward) saves a forkpoint once the body produced a value.
